title: TWA 6 (1935)
summary: TWA Flight 6 descended toward an emergency landing field due to worsening weather and fuel concerns. The crew flew under a low cloud ceiling at very low level in darkness over fog-shrouded terrain when the aircraft's wingtip struck the ground. Investigators attributed the accident to multiple factors including communications malfunctions, darkness, inaccurate weather forecasts, and errors in judgment by airline dispatchers and flight crew. Five of thirteen occupants were killed.
probable_cause: Several factors contributed including communications malfunctions, darkness, inaccurate weather forecasts, worsening weather at the destination airport, and errors in judgment from both the airline dispatchers and the flight crew.

title: Medellin plane crash of 1935
summary: Two Ford Trimotor aircraft collided at Olaya Herrera Airport in Medellín Colombia on June 24 1935. SACO F-31 was taking off with 13 occupants including Argentine tango singer Carlos Gardel when it suddenly started to swerve and lose control. The aircraft veered off the runway and collided with taxiing aircraft C-31 causing an explosion that engulfed both planes in flames. Investigation revealed strong lateral winds combined with runway surface irregularities caused F-31 to lose control.
probable_cause: Loss of control during takeoff due to strong lateral winds combined with runway surface irregularities resulting in collision with taxiing aircraft.

title: 1935 San Giacomo Douglas DC-2 crash
summary: A Douglas DC-2 encountered severe thunderstorms and heavy rain while flying over the Swiss Alps, causing rapid icing on the airframe. The pilot descended to gain visibility but lost altitude faster than expected when engine power was reduced. After flying in circles for over 20 minutes searching for a valley exit, the pilot attempted an emergency landing on hilly terrain but the aircraft tilted forward and crashed, killing all 13 occupants.
probable_cause: Severe weather with high altitude icing and low visibility combined with inadequate terrain clearance during the emergency landing attempt.

factors.evidence: While flying over the pass, the plane encountered severe weather with heavy thunderstorms, torrential rain and drop in temperature.
Due to icing and bad weather, the plane had to descend when it flew over the Alps. Very strong icing suddenly occurred.
Due to clouds, the pilot was not able to exit the valley via the north exit. The pilot turned and attempted to exit the valley via the southern exit, but this also failed.

While flying above San Bernardino they reported over the radio 'we have to deal with heavy rain and dense fog'. Presumably because the exit was completely shrouded in mist, the pilot saw no other option than to make an emergency landing.

With the skills of the pilot, he succeeded in obtaining ground visibility at an altitude of around 1600 meters. With the engines off, flaps extended and landing gear retracted, he made a belly landing on highly hilly terrain.
The plane flew in circles in the valley to find an exit for over 20 minutes and the pilot descended further to gain visibility. The landing failed and the plane broke in half.

events.text: Aircraft departed Milan at 11:56am local time for Frankfurt, flying over Switzerland to Schiphol, Amsterdam.
Aircraft encountered severe thunderstorms with torrential rain and heavy icing at altitude over the San Bernardino pass.
Pilot descended to gain visibility after being unable to exit the valley via the north pass due to clouds.
Pilot reported over radio 'I'm flying blind and looking for my position' and 'we have to deal with heavy rain and dense fog'.
Pilot attempted emergency landing on hilly terrain just outside San Giacomo at 12:30, with engines off, flaps extended and landing gear retracted.
Aircraft tilted forward during left turn before landing and crashed to the ground, breaking in half and crushing from front to back.

title: United Airlines 4
summary: A Boeing 247D in night conditions failed to maintain altitude during descent near Cheyenne airport. The aircraft struck the ground in a shallow descent just below a knoll. The captain, despite extensive experience on the route, did not monitor altitude or location. Darkness and speculative fog, combined with cockpit lights set to maximum intensity which reduced external visibility, contributed to spatial disorientation.
probable_cause: Pilot error in failing to monitor altitude or location, compounded by darkness, possible sleep deprivation of the captain, and fog.

events.text: The aircraft last contacted Cheyenne at 02:16 or 02:17 local time, reporting its position as Silver Crown beacon.
At 2:00 a.m. the weather at the Cheyenne airport was recorded as clear with ceiling unlimited, air temperature of 41.7F, and winds out of the northwest at 9 miles per hour.
According to the accident report, the cockpit lights were set to maximum intensity at the time of the crash, which reduces visibility outside the aircraft during night flight.
The aircraft struck the ground in a shallow descent just below a small knoll at elevation of 6,553 ft.
